messages:
maya: Quick sync — posting a few variants for the Spend overview layout. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx — want focused feedback on: scope toggle (Org vs Project), token breakdown density, and where the invoice download CTA should live.

sam: Saw the frames — nice baseline. Two immediate things: the left-scope rail feels heavy, and the sparkline+stack maybe competes with the token donut. Might need a clear visual hierarchy.

ellie: Agree with Sam. Also accessibility nit: the contrast on the token donut labels is 3.8:1 right now. We should hit 4.5:1 for normal text or 3:1 for large text. Can we try bolder label color?

noah: Copy suggestion for the scope toggle — current "Account / Project" reads like a noun list. How about "View by: Organization / Project"? More explicit.

maya: Good call on copy. Also thinking about default scope based on user role: org-admin sees Org by default; project-product sees Project. Should we surface that choice in the UI or keep it inferred?

sam: Prefer inferred default but show a subtle badge: "Viewing: Organization" with a keyboard-focusable toggle to switch. That reduces friction.

design-bot: Reminder: run axe-core checks on the new layout before next demo.

ellie: Interaction notes: keyboard nav between scope toggle and the sparkline must be logical. If toggle is first element, hitting Tab should land on the date range selector next, not the chart. Also charts need descriptive aria-labels ex: aria-label="Spend chart: last 30 days, grouped by model".

noah: On token breakdown — compact grid (3 cols) looks dense on wide screens. Maybe a responsive approach: 3 cols desktop, 1 col mobile, 2 col tablet. Also add a tooltip on hover for "Tokens billed" that explains token vs prompt/response split.

maya: What about the invoice CTA? Options: 1) primary button in top-right of panel, 2) small link next to "Billing period" header, 3) dented card action inside ledger list. Thoughts?

sam: 1 feels too dominant — invoice download is important but not primary action compared to model switch or timeframe. I like 2: near the period header with a discrete button: `Download invoice` (secondary).

ellie: From an accessibility POV, put the download link in the header as a real button (not an anchor-only) so keyboard users can find it in the logical heading flow. Also ensure aria-describedby points to invoice status text (e.g., "Processing" or "Ready").

noah: Performance thought: the donut + sparkline currently re-renders on hover causing jank. Let's virtualize the tooltip layer and avoid reflowing SVG elements. Eng-runtime can help with a shallow redraw.

maya: Yep, will sync with eng-runtime. Also want to discuss the compact token list copy: current labels like "Prompt Tokens" vs "Input Tokens" — inconsistent. Proposal: use "Prompt (tokens)" and "Response (tokens)" and show a small info icon linking to billing docs.

sam: +1. Make sure the info icon has accessible text: aria-label="What counts as a prompt token".

ellie: Minor visual tweak: increase tappable area for the donut legend to 44x44px. Mobile tests showed misses on small hands.

maya: For the scope switch animation — let's avoid an animation longer than 120ms. Keep it subtle. Also ensure reduced-motion respects OS setting.

noah: UX question: should we allow pinning a default scope per user? e.g., a small star action on the scope toggle. That would help heavy project users.

sam: Love that. If we add pinning, ensure it's discoverable but not noisy. Maybe a tooltip on hover: "Pin this view as default".

ellie: Final accessibility pass items for next week: contrast, keyboard order, hit target sizes, aria-labels, reduced-motion. I'll compile a quick checklist.

maya: Thanks team. Action items: ellie -> accessibility checklist, noah -> perf tweaks with eng-runtime, sam -> implement copy & small CTA placement, maya -> update Figma with scoped variants and pinning mock. We'll reconvene Thursday. :thumbsup:
